states.text: engine.py:44 drops the Authorization header when following a redirect, leaking credentials to third-party hosts.
The code quality could be better in several places.
nodes/script.py crashes with KeyError 'stdout' when the adapter subprocess is killed by a signal before producing output.
Error handling is inconsistent across the codebase.
storage/db.py:112 builds the SQL query with string formatting, so a user-supplied folder name can inject arbitrary SQL.
Some functions are too long and should probably be refactored.
The README install instructions reference requirements.txt, but the project moved to pyproject.toml, so a fresh contributor following them fails.
Pricing calculation sometimes returns the wrong total for edge cases.
worker.py:88 calls asyncio.create_task without keeping a reference, so fire-and-forget tasks can be garbage-collected mid-flight and silently disappear.
auth/session.py:201 writes the session token to a world-readable file, so any local user on the box can steal active sessions.
Naming is confusing in a few of the newer modules.
The API feels slow under heavy load.
parsers/csv.py raises csv.Error('field larger than field limit') on any row over 131072 characters; the limit is neither raised nor configurable.
It would be nice to add more tests.
api/handlers.py:77 reads the full request body into memory without checking content_length first, so one 10GB upload OOMs the pod.
The design feels over-engineered in places.
The config loader silently falls back to defaults when the YAML file is malformed, instead of failing loudly.
Users report occasional crashes in production.
utils.py:5 defines two functions named _normalize; the later definition shadows the first, so callers of the first get the wrong implementation.
Docstrings are missing throughout the newer modules.
